newsitem.title: UK: Portugal's Franco upbeat on inflation, deficit.
newsitem.headline: Portugal's Franco upbeat on inflation, deficit.

text.p: Portuguese Finance Minister Antonio Sousa Franco said on Wednesday that provisional estimates for March inflation and first quarter 1997 public finance targets were better than expected.

"We have first estimates of inflation concerning March -- very provisional...but they are better than we had foreseen," Franco said in an interview with Reuters Financial Television (RFTV), due to be broadcast later on Wednesday.
Asked if he was worried about robust growth this year leading to inflationary pressures, Franco said, "I don't see any factors that would have a strong inflationary impact."

He said public revenue and spending targets for the first three months of this year had been exceeded and no new measures were thus needed to make the 2.9 percent deficit to gross domestic product (GDP) forecast for Portugal in 1997.
The Maastricht Treaty sets out a three percent deficit to GDP requirement for countries wishing to take part in European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).
"We only have results of the first three months. The results are very good from an expenditure and a receipts side," Franco said. "We had targets for those months and they have been exceeded."

He said Portugal collected more receipts than expected and spending was held to levels predicted. "I don't see a need for any additional discretionary measures to achieve the 2.9 percent but should they be necessary of course they would be approved."
Asked whether the Portuguese 10-year yield spread against German Bunds could get back down to the 80 basis point level reached in January, Franco said the trend was for a reduction in the spread.

"The spread (narrowing previously) was based on the confidence that we could be, as we are going to be, in the first group, phase three of EMU," he said. "The trend is for supported reductions of the spread."
Phase three of EMU, under which the single euro currency is due to be introduced, is scheduled for January 1, 1999.
The Portuguese/Bund spread at 1159 GMT was 109 basis points.
In February, Portugal's consumer price index rose 0.2 percent for a 2.9 percent year-on-year rate, or 3.2 percent on the rolling 12-month average.
That compared with a 0.3 percent gain in January when the year-on-year rate was 3.3 percent and the rolling average was 3.2 percent.
When the data were released, in mid-March, analysts said they meant the government's goal of bringing the average figure down to 2.25-to-2.50 percent was possible.
Franco said on Wednesday that 2.50 percent would be "reasonable".
